H&M Earnings Rise as Cost-Saving Push Pays Off
STOCKHOLM--Hennes & Mauritz reported higher quarterly earnings as the fast-fashion retailer's efforts to cut costs and improve efficiency continued to boost profitability.

The Swedish company said sales in its fiscal third quarter--which runs from June through August--rose 1% in local currencies, just above a UBS forecast looking for 0.7%, as summer collections were well received.

The positive sales development came despite continued disruptions in the logistics network in Europe and in the global supply chain, and there remains potential for sales to increase going forward, the company said.
The company said sales in September, the first month of its fourth quarter, are expected to increase by 1% in local currencies on year.

H&M reported an operating profit of 6.04 billion Swedish kronor ($608.9 million) for the third quarter through Aug. 31 compared with 4.91 billion kronor a year earlier as reported sales rose 0.3% to 57.19 billion kronor. Analysts polled by FactSet had expected operating profit of 5.52 billion kronor on sales of 57.09 billion kronor.
Operating profit was supported by one-time effects related to tariffs and goods imports that had increased the cost of goods sold in previous quarters, it added.
